Commentary.Commentary: Right. Pakistan kick off their new era under Mike Hesson in style, securing a dominant win to take a 1-0 lead in this three-match T20I series. Meanwhile, Bangladesh faces an early setback and will need to regroup, reassess, and find a way to bounce back. With momentum on Pakistan’s side, the tourists will be desperate to level the series. That wraps up the series opener, and all eyes now turn to the second T20I, which will be played on 30th May, Friday, with action set to begin at 3 pm GMT, with Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium being the exclusive venue for this series. But, be sure to tune in an hour early for all the buildup. See you then, take care!

The captain of Pakistan, Salman Agha, reflects that they made a strong comeback after losing two wickets on just 5 runs. Says this is what they want from this side. Adds they want to do well in all three departments and want people to come and take the game on. On Hasan Ali's five-for, Agha says that he appreciates his performance and says it is good to see the Hasan Ali of 2017 back in form. Mentions that he has worked very hard off the field and is happy to see it paying off well for him. Also highlights his good showing in the PSL as well. On being asked about the all-rounders in the side, Salman considers it a luxury to have. Also points that they have Saim Ayub as well, who can bowl four overs. About the next game, he says they will take a bit of rest before preparing for the second game.

The captain of Bangladesh, Litton Das, reflects on the defeat. He says that he is disappointed that they could not build on the good start. Adds that they didn't bat, bowl, or field well in this game and need to be more consistent. Mentions that 200 was definitely chasable at this ground as the wicket was good too. Says that they did not bat well in the middle overs, but praises Jaker Ali for his effort and says that he has been good for a long time now. Ends by saying that he believes that they need to have a clear mindset for the next games and come back mentally rather than in practice.

Shadab Khan of Pakistan is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his all-round brilliance on the field. He says that his comeback wasn't great, but he worked really hard, and the PSL went well for him, and it gave him a lot of confidence. Mentions that his bowling was going well, but there are several areas that need improvement going forward. Shares that the ball was not coming onto the bat, so his plan was to bowl short of length and keep away from the batter.
It is time for the Presentation ceremony...

Pakistan's Hasan Ali, the man of the moment says that the thought was simple, to hit the right areas as they know the conditions well. Adds that the batters also played well to put up 200 runs, which allowed them to execute their plans well. Mentions that variations are key in T20s as it has become easier for the batters, and changing pace and using different variations are important. Says that he can't ask for anything else, it is special to take a fifer on his return to the team. Further adds that the rehab was boring, but you need to have dedication and hunger. He also thanks the PCB and physios for working with him, as it was a career-threatening injury. Tells that Mike Hesson said that they need to play modern cricket and they have seen how the world is playing this format, and they wanted to execute their plans which they did in this game.

Earlier in the game, after electing to bat first, Pakistan’s innings stumbled early at 5/2, losing both openers in the first six. But skipper Salman Agha and Mohammad Haris steadied the ship, with Agha leading the charge. His blazing fifty proved crucial, as he built vital partnerships, first with Haris, then Hasan Nawaz, keeping Pakistan dominant in the middle overs. The aggressive intent of the incoming batters ensured momentum stayed on their side. Shadab Khan and Hasan Nawaz’s late contributions pushed Pakistan beyond the 200-run mark. Every bowler of Bangladesh shared wickets, with Shoriful Islam bagging two to his name, while the rest chipped in with one apiece.

Jaker Ali fought to keep Bangladesh’s hopes alive with some powerful hits, but the chase had already slipped beyond reach. With too many runs left for the final stretch and not enough wickets in hand, the task proved insurmountable. After his dismissal, they got wrapped up in a flash. Hasan Ali replicated his PSL magic with a crucial five-wicket haul, and while Haris Rauf was a bit expensive, the rest of the bowling attack played their part, picking up wickets at the right moments to seal a well-earned victory.

Bangladesh found some rhythm with a 63-run stand, but just as Litton Das and Tawhid Hridoy looked ready to shift gears, disaster struck. First, skipper Litton Das fell, then Hridoy followed, triggering a dramatic collapse. From a steady 100/2, the visitors tumbled to 124/6, losing all their key batters in quick succession. The spinners seized control, with Shadab Khan leading the charge, stamping Pakistan’s authority on the game.

Bangladesh’s chase of 202 got off to a rocky start, losing both openers early, but Tanzid Hasan provided some stability before falling. Hasan Ali and company tightened their grip, leaving Bangladesh at 45/2 by the Powerplay, trailing Pakistan’s 52/2 at the same stage. Litton Das and Tawhid Hridoy then took charge, carefully rebuilding the innings, but spinners Shadab Khan and Abrar Ahmed kept them in check, restricting boundaries and allowing only 30 runs in the next four overs after the Powerplay, though without conceding a wicket.

A job well done by Pakistan across all departments. A commanding performance in all facets of the game, first setting the tone with the bat by surpassing the 200-run mark, then reinforcing their dominance with the ball. Meanwhile, Bangladesh had a tough start to the series, completely outplayed by Pakistan’s formidable force in Lahore.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Abrar Ahmed to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls the length back, does Abrar, drifting on the pads, this is clipped away to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Abrar Ahmed to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding down on the pads, Litton Das clips it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Abrar Ahmed to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: From over the wicket. dragged length, on the off stump, Litton Das tucks it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Abrar Ahmed to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and on off, takes off a bit, Litton Das steers it wide of short third. The ball skids through, but Faheem Ashraf dives to his left to make a fine stop. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Haris Rauf to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, angling into the batter, Tawhid Hridoy pulls it to mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Haris Rauf to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a short length, angling in, Tawhid Hridoy defends it on the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Haris Rauf to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Tawhid Hridoy dabs it to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Haris Rauf to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a short length, on the stumps, Tawhid Hridoy pulls that one to deep backward square leg, Hasan Nawaz fumbles there, and the batters complete the second run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Haris Rauf to Tawhid Hridoy, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: From over the wicket, on the back of a length, angling into the batter, Litton Das tucks it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Haris Rauf to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a short length, outside off, lifting off the deck. Litton Das climbs on the bounce and taps it out to the point region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, shaping away, Tawhid Hridoy strides across and plays the cover drive. The fielder inside the circle at cover, dives to his right and makes a half stop. It is parried around mid off and the batters cross over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Faheem Ashraf to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, on the pads, nudged to the right of mid-wicket. Khushdil Shah makes a sharp diving stop to his right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Faheem Ashraf to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, almost carried back to the bowler. A gentle-paced delivery, on a length, and nipping back into the batter. Tawhid Hridoy hops and looks to tuck into the leg side, but closes the bat face early. The ball goes straight off the leading edge, dipping low to the right of the bowler. Ashraf dives and sticks his right hand out, but the ball evades him and rolls into the mid on region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Faheem Ashraf to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length, across off, Das cuts it square through backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, around off, punched to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tawhid Hridoy comes out to the middle now.

OUT! OUTFOXED! CLEANED HIM UP! What a roaring comeback from Hasan Ali! An off cutter by the looks of it, bang on target, around off, on a fullish length. Tanzid Hasan is a bit early to swing through as he looks to loft it over mid-wicket. The ball keeps shaping in and arrives late on the batter and sneaks through the gap between bat and pad, to disturb the timber. The off pole is uprooted. Tanzid Hasan departs after a fine start - 31 (17). Bangladesh are now 37/2.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, OUT! b Hasan Ali.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! More runs! Nagging length, on top of middle, Tanzid Hasan shimmies down the track and flat bats it over the bowler for a boundary straight down the ground.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: TOP EDGE, FOUR! Bowls an effort ball, does Ali, short and climbing on the left shoulder of the batter. Tanzid Hasan is not in complete control as he shapes to pull, but gets a top edge and the ball flies over the keeper for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent stuff from Hasan Ali! A pace-off delivery, curving back into the batter, on middle and leg, Tanzid Hasan is cramped for room and just manages to fend it onto the surface.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled across off, on a length, Tanzid Hasan gets on the toes and guides it to the backward point region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, skidding of the deck, on top of middle and leg, Tanzid Hasan gets across and tucks it straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower through the air, a leg break, turning away from off, Litton Das hangs back and knocks it to the right of the bowler. Abrar Ahmed dives to his right and stops the ball. A 15-run opening over from Abrar.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Abrar Ahmed to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A slider on the middle stump, tossed up fuller, Litton Das gets a bit across and taps it in the pocket between mid on and mid-wicket for a couple of runs. The man from long on mops it up to his right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Abrar Ahmed to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags the length back around off, Tanzid Hasan hangs back and tucks it wide of long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Abrar Ahmed to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up, floated full and on off, pushed to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Abrar Ahmed to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! TWO IN TWO FOR TANZID! Another half volley served right into the wheelhouse, at the stumps. Tanzid Hasan with a gentle tap on the front foot, lifts it straight up and over the sightscreen for another half a dozen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Abrar Ahmed to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Goes all the way! Serves a friendly half volley on middle, does Abrar, Tanzid Hasan gets forward and lofts it over the bowler for a cracking six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Abrar Ahmed to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Skipper Litton Das walks out to bat at number 3 Also, time for some mystery spin as Abrar Ahmed comes into the attack.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! The slower one does the trick for Hasan Ali and he continues his form from the PSL! He dishes out a slower ball, and lands it fuller, with a hint of shape into the batter, on the leg stump line. Parvez Hossain Emon tilts forward to whip it over the mid-wicket region, but is early through his shot. Ends up hitting it off the toe-end of the bat and the ball spoons up, and straight down the throat of Haris Rauf at mid on. He is not dropping those. Bangladesh lose their first wicket on 14 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Haris Rauf b Hasan Ali
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Hasan Ali to Parvez Hossain Emon, OUT! c Haris Rauf b Hasan Ali.

Commentary.Commentary: Wild swing and a miss! Pitched short and outside off, Parvez Hossain Emon swivels to pull but the ball keeps angling away from him and he is beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Hasan Ali to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An off cutter, across off, on a length, tapped away to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Hasan Ali to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, just short of Haris Rauf, but a brave effort there from him. An inswinger from Hasan Ali, on middle and curving on the leg stump line, full in length. Emon is a bit early into the flick shot and ends up chipping it in the air, in front of mid on where the ball dips in front of Haris Rauf. He bends low to his left and almost scoops the ball. The umpires want to have a check for a fair catch, but the replay shows that the ball just bumped before the fingers of Rauf.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Hasan Ali to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Is that out? Haris Rauf claims the catch and puts up his fingers, but the umpires want to take a look. Rauf has also hurt his fingers a bit while trying to grab it. The replay clearly shows that the ball bounces before going into his hands. It is Not Out.
Around off, on a nagging length, Tanzid Hasan works this behind square on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a full delivery, around off, angling across, Tanzid Hasan with a good-looking cover drive, plays it through cover-point. Saim Ayub runs across to his left from deep backward point and intercepts it with a slide. Just two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Hasan Ali to Tanzid Hasan, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hasan Ali to share the attack.

FOUR! A bit streaky, but he will take it! An expensive start from Faheem Ashraf as 11 runs come off the opening over! Speared in fuller, just outside off. Parvez Hossain Emon looks to loft it over cover, but gets a thick outside edge and the ball flies to the right of backward point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Faheem Ashraf to Parvez Hossain Emon, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Across off, on a short length, Tanzid Hasan gets down the track and slashes it hard, but straight to the cover fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Faheem Ashraf to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! What a way to get off the mark! Just back of a length, jagging back in on the leg stump, Tanzid Hasan weighs on the back foot and just picks it up and over square leg, with an aerial whip for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Faheem Ashraf to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, on the leg stump line, skidding through. Tanzid Hasan is hurried to play the pull and misses. The ball lobs off his thigh pad and goes straight towards the short fine leg fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Faheem Ashraf to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, around off, punched down to the left of mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Faheem Ashraf to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right on the money! A bit full and on off, sliced away straight to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Faheem Ashraf to Tanzid Hasan, No run.
